name: Lichen
desc: Crustose lichen colonies creep across dark granite — sulphur-yellow, rust-orange, sage and near-black species each stopping dead where they touch a neighbour, so a hard seam opens between them and the raised living margins glow around every territory, laying zonation rings as they age and dying out from the necrotic centre to free the stone for fresh propagules, the whole mosaic swelling and saturating as moisture cycles.

energy.doc: growth rate, thallus swell and colour saturation

density.doc: how many colonies contend for the rock (6-22) and the weight of the margins/seams

hue.doc: base hue — the four species are offsets from it, so this rotates the whole mosaic while keeping them distinct

speed.doc: rate of growth, ageing and the moisture cycle

scale.doc: maximum colony radius — from a fine crust to a few huge contending plates

wobble.doc: how ragged the thallus outline is — clean discs to lobed crusts

act.doc: cycle: moisture comes and goes · flush: permanently wet, swollen and saturated · desiccate: dried out, shrunken and dull

style.doc: specimen: saturated species colour on dark granite · plate: botanical engraving, form from radial hatching · map: flat coded lithology, hard boundaries, no modelling at all · nocturne: UV fluorescence — the colonies glow off a near-black rock
